summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease s/p CABG, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for acute chest pain radiating to the neck and left arm. Initial concern for myocardial infarction was mitigated by imaging showing no acute blockage or aortic dissection, suggesting an aborted event. During her stay, she was treated for uncontrolled diabetes with increased insulin dosing and transition to an insulin pen. Chronic kidney disease stage III, attributed to diabetic and hypertensive nephropathy, was monitored and managed. Gastritis was addressed with antacids, and shoulder pain from degenerative joint changes was noted. Social work was involved due to her history of noncompliance and lack of home support. She was discharged with home health services, medication adjustments, and follow-up arranged with cardiology, endocrinology, and primary care.
